xmltvId.doc: The id set on the channel (unset channels use their Volt id)

source_name.doc: Name of the channel or event, or the title of the library asset

kind.doc: channel (live source), event, or fast_channel (built from the library)

on_air.doc: published: a channel on air, an event live

stale.doc: The asset has changed since this copy went out

platform.doc: portal, youtube, facebook, x, tiktok, dailymotion, instagram or threads

kind.doc: How the capture is sliced: one run per event, or one per channel per day

day_utc.doc: The UTC day of a channel-day recording

token_prefix.doc: The first characters of the link token, to recognise a link

source_name.doc: The channel or event it was cut from

schema_key.doc: Standard content type key (episode, movie, clip, sports-match ...)

schema_org_type.doc: schema.org type of the content type (Episode, Movie, VideoObject, SportsEvent ...)

origin.doc: How it was made: recording, clip, upload or watchfolder

source.doc: What it belongs to: channel, event, radio, upload, or none (its channel or event is gone)

metadata_missing_required.doc: A required target field is empty, or the asset has no content type

has_stale_publication.doc: A published copy is older than this asset

usage_status.doc: Can it be used: ready, unchecked, qc_failed, processing, failed, unplayable or no_media. Only ready is offered to FAST, loops and blocking

object_key.doc: The file path in the folder

status.doc: seen, ingested, quarantined, failed, reprocessed or removed

hook.doc: The hook that started it ('manual' for a hand run)
